title: “Furthermore, Meghiya, for a monk well established in these five things, four more things are to be developed: foulness should be developed to abandon greed;…
content: “Furthermore, Meghiya, for a monk well established in these five things, four more things are to be developed: foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon ill-will; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot the conceit ‘I am.’ For one with the perception of impermanence, Meghiya, the perception of not-self becomes established. For one with the perception of not-self, the uprooting of the conceit ‘I am’ is attained, Nibbāna in this very life.”

title: “Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms. Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s body thrown in the charnel ground, one, two, or…
content:
“Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms. Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s body thrown in the charnel ground, one, two, or three days dead – bloated, discolored, festering. What do you think, monks? Has the former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?”
“Yes, venerable sir.”
“Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline, as fewness of wishes. For one…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline, as fewness of wishes. For one with few wishes, monks, unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline.”

title: “And, monks, when that monk dwells in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to abandon…
content: “And, monks, when that monk dwells in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon ill-will; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot the conceit ‘I am.’ For a monk with the perception of impermanence, monks, the perception of not-self becomes established. For one with the perception of not-self, the conceit ‘I am’ is uprooted, and Nibbāna is attained in this very life.”

title: Standing to one side, the deity Candana recited this verse to the Blessed One: How can one cross the flood, Steadfast and persevering day and…
content:
Standing to one side, the deity Candana recited this verse to the Blessed One:
How can one cross the flood,
Steadfast and persevering day and night?
Without stalling, without clinging —
Who does not sink in the abyss?

(The Blessed One):
One who always has virtue,
Wisdom, and is well-concentrated,
With aroused energy and strength —
That one crosses the hard-to-cross flood.
One who has abandoned perception of lust,
Who has crossed beyond the fetter of form,
Who has destroyed delight and craving for existence —
That one does not sink in the abyss.

title: "The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and…
content: "The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. He drenches, saturates, fills, and pervades his very body with the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, so that no spot on his entire body is not pervaded by that rapture and pleasure born of seclusion."

title: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment.…
content: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. Udāyi, I say: ‘This person is not bound, not fettered.’ Why is that? Udāyi, the difference in his faculties has been fully understood by me.”

title: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or…
content: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old — aged, bent like a roof, crooked, leaning on a staff, trembling as she walks, sick, her youth exhausted, teeth broken, hair grey, bald, wrinkled, limbs shriveled and pale. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

title: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” -…
content: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Brahmin, being infatuated by craving, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both, and experiences mental suffering and mental distress. When craving is abandoned, one does not plan for one’s own harm, nor for others’ harm, nor for the harm of both, and does not experience mental suffering or mental distress. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one engages in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. When craving is abandoned, one does not engage in misconduct of body, speech, or mind. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one does not know as it actually is one’s own benefit, nor the benefit of others, nor the benefit of both. When craving is abandoned, one knows as it actually is one’s own benefit, the benefit of others, and the benefit of both. Thus, brahmin, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — A collection of many diseases, impure, Full of stench, rotting. Develop your mind, Contemplate the…
content:
Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
A collection of many diseases, impure,
Full of stench, rotting.
Develop your mind,
Contemplate the nature of foulness,
Achieve one-pointedness,
With mind well concentrated.

Practice the signless,
Abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.
By fully understanding conceit,
You will live at peace.
